memory_update.text: Layer 1B universe for advanced_compute_packaging_memory_networking should include direct accelerator vendors NVDA and AMD, but should not stop there; AVGO, TSM, MU, MRVL, ANET and AMAT are important second-order mappings.

The strongest chokepoint claims in this node are likely to center on HBM supply, advanced packaging capacity, advanced-node foundry capacity, custom ASIC/networking silicon and scale-out Ethernet switching.

Potential future additions outside the 8-candidate cap include ASML, Lam Research, KLA, Teradyne, Amkor, Coherent, Lumentum, Fabrinet, Super Micro Computer and Celestica, depending on whether Layer 2 focuses more on lithography, test, optics, OSAT, or rack integration.

Substrate makers and some OSAT/advanced-packaging specialists are less represented among large US-listed equities; non-US listings may be required for fuller coverage of ABF substrates, CoWoS ecosystem suppliers and HBM peers.

node: Accelerated compute stack: AI accelerators, advanced packaging, HBM, substrates, high-speed interconnect and AI networking
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the AI accelerated-compute supply-chain node. The shortlist emphasizes companies with direct exposure to AI accelerators, advanced-node foundry and packaging capacity, HBM memory, AI networking silicon, Ethernet switching, and semiconductor equipment. The central Layer 1B hypothesis remains that market attention may concentrate on accelerator brands while second-order chokepoints such as HBM supply, CoWoS/advanced packaging, custom ASIC connectivity, and process equipment may also capture durable economics if AI cluster demand persists.
